title: U.S. House · Florida's 20th District
area: Parts of Broward County, including Weston and surrounding South Florida communities, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.

Incumbent Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Luther Campbell, Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, Dale Holness, and Elijah Manley. Brent Andersen won the Republican primary. Kedner Maxime advanced as the Independent Party of Florida nominee after that primary was canceled.

summary.text: Debbie Wasserman Schultz is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative, first sworn into the House in 2005 after eight years in the Florida House and four in the Florida Senate. She chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016 and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. She is running for re-election in the 20th District.

background.text: Born in Queens, New York, in 1966; graduated from Half Hollow Hills High School East in 1984.
Attended the University of Florida, where her official biography says she was president of the Student Senate, and earned a bachelor's degree (1988) and a master's degree (1990) in political science.
Worked as a staffer to U.S. Representative Peter Deutsch (D) before running for office.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1992 to 2000 and the Florida Senate from 2000 to 2004.
First sworn into the U.S. House in 2005. Her official biography describes her as Florida's first Jewish congresswoman.
Chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Agriculture, Energy and Water, and Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittees in the 119th Congress). Her official biography says she was the first woman to chair the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Subcommittee, in the 117th Congress, and that she co-chairs the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee in the 119th Congress.

Her official biography lists legislation she authored or sponsored, including the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act (2007), the PROTECT Our Children Act (2007), the EARLY Act (enacted in 2010 as part of the Affordable Care Act), and the Rape Survivor Child Custody Act (signed in 2015).
Advanced from the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for the 20th District. According to her official biography, she is married to Steve Schultz and they have three children.

priorities.text: Says increasing access to higher education and improving college affordability have been a top priority throughout her legislative career, including continued support for robust Pell grant funding and legislation allowing students to refinance loans at low rates.

Says addressing gun violence as a public health crisis is a priority, including closing background-check loopholes, banning the sale of assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, and funding CDC research on gun violence.

Says she uses her position as a senior appropriator on the Energy and Water Appropriations Subcommittee to support a national energy strategy promoting a rapid transition to clean, renewable, domestic energy sources.

positions.summary: Says Congress should close background-check loopholes for gun and ammunition purchases and ban the sale of assault weapons and high-capacity magazines.
positions.quote: We should start by closing all the background check loopholes that allow dangerous people to evade the law and purchase deadly firearms.

positions.summary: Says efforts to repeal or defund the Affordable Care Act are not productive and cites its coverage and subsidy gains for Floridians.
positions.quote: efforts to repeal or defund the ACA are not productive in working toward quality, more affordable healthcare for all Americans.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to a pathway to citizenship and protections for DREAMers, Temporary Protected Status holders, and refugees, and has sponsored or cosponsored bills to protect DACA and TPS recipients.
positions.quote: This includes providing a pathway to citizenship, fair treatment under the law, and extending protections for DREAMers, Temporary Protected Status holders, and refugees.

positions.summary: Says she supports a national energy strategy for a rapid transition to clean, renewable energy sources to address the climate crisis, while opposing offshore oil and gas drilling.
positions.quote: I believe it is critical that we use smart, forward-thinking energy policy to address the climate crisis and prevent the worst consequences of climate change by dramatically reducing our emissions of greenhouse gases.

positions.summary: Says she will defend the right to abortion services.
positions.quote: I will always defend this right, including access to abortion services, for women here at home and around the world as a principle tenet of women’s comprehensive health.

positions.summary: Says she cosponsored legislation to raise the federal minimum wage and tipped minimum wage to $15.
positions.quote: I have cosponsored legislation to raise the federal minimum wage and tipped minimum wage to 15 dollars by 2020.

record.text: Sits on the House Appropriations Committee for the 2025–2026 Congress, including its Agriculture and Energy and Water subcommittees.
Authored the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act, enacted in 2007, and sponsored the PROTECT Our Children Act, creating a federal law enforcement effort to protect children.
Introduced the EARLY Act to increase breast cancer education and awareness, which was enacted as part of the Affordable Care Act in 2010.
Introduced the Rape Survivor Child Custody Act, encouraging states to allow termination of a rapist's parental rights; signed into law in 2015.

candidates.name: Brent Andersen

summary.text: Brent Andersen is a Pompano Beach insurance agency founder and Republican Party leader who won the Republican primary for the 20th District on August 18, 2026. He describes himself as a conservative businessman and says he is running on lowering property insurance costs and the cost of living.

background.text: Says he was raised in a middle-class family, the son of a public school teacher and a union asbestos worker.
Earned a high school diploma from Saint John's High School and a bachelor's degree from Nichols College in 2000, according to Ballotpedia; says his degree is a B.S. in Finance.
Says he founded Pilgrim Bay Insurance Agency in 2010, a commercial brokerage serving New England and Southeast Florida; Ballotpedia lists his career as insurance broker.
Describes himself as a lifelong Republican who spent two decades in party leadership roles and held gubernatorial appointments in higher education and state finance.
Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 53.8% of the vote, ahead of Rod Joseph, Carla Spalding, and Lateresa Jones.
Says he lives in Pompano Beach with his wife, Yula, and their young daughter, and lists endorsements from the Sun Sentinel, Miami Herald, and Log Cabin Republicans PAC.

priorities.text: Says his experience in the insurance industry drives his focus on market-based solutions to lower property insurance premiums and housing costs.
Says he will bring private-sector experience and fiscal responsibility to Congress to grow jobs and economic opportunity.
Says he will defend limited government, the Second Amendment, secure borders, and parental rights.

positions.summary: Said in an Aug. 2026 interview that he is firmly pro-life.

statements.quote: Sí, apoyo la Segunda Enmienda. No se puede cambiar la Constitución sin una enmienda constitucional. Ahora bien, si hubiera restricciones razonables para que la gente mala no tenga armas, sí, por supuesto.
statements.context: Spanish-language interview with Diario las Américas, Aug. 2, 2026

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia survey and an Aug. 2, 2026 Spanish-language Diario las Américas interview reviewed (quotes appear in Spanish as published). No campaign website found.

candidates.name: Kedner Maxime
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Independent Party of Florida nominee after that primary was canceled

summary.text: Kedner Maxime is the Independent Party of Florida nominee in the general election for Florida's 20th District. His campaign website lists issue pages on costs, immigration, healthcare and education.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Port-de-Paix, Haiti, and came to the United States in April 1981 at age 18 as a student.
Says his first jobs in the U.S. were washing dishes and mowing golf courses, sometimes working three jobs at once.

According to his campaign website, he completed a GED at Dillard High School, an associate degree in business administration at Broward College, and a bachelor's degree in business administration at Nova Southeastern University. He was ordained in 2011 with a Master of Theology and holds a Doctor of Divinity from Liberty Bible School & Seminary.
Founded Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services in 1996, where he says he works as an accountant and immigration consultant.
Says he has been a pastor for 16 years at L'Eglise la Voix du Salut and has hosted the Tass Cafe Show on WLQY 1320AM for 20 years.

Advanced to the general election as the Independent Party of Florida nominee after that party's August 18, 2026 primary was canceled. His campaign website says he married in 1984 and has two children and a granddaughter.

priorities.text: Lower costs: housing, groceries and healthcare.
priorities.quote: Support responsible federal spending and fair competition that brings inflation down and stops price gouging.

priorities.text: Healthcare: lower prescription drug costs and protect coverage for people with pre-existing conditions.
priorities.quote: Protect coverage for people with pre-existing conditions

priorities.text: Education: raise public-school funding and teacher salaries.
priorities.quote: Raise public-school funding so classrooms have the resources, materials, and support they need.

statements.quote: Deportation of those who commit crimes.
statements.context: One of six items on his campaign immigration page, which also lists secure borders and a pathway to citizenship for those who contribute

statements.quote: Expand access to affordable care for working families, the self-employed, and small-business owners.
Expand affordable housing so working families, seniors, and young people can find a home they can actually afford.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website issue pages (costs, immigration, healthcare, education) reviewed. The site states no position on abortion, guns or other tracked issues.
